translations.idiomatic: On renzi, ritual officials were ordered to deliberate the Jin ruler’s honorific title.

sentences.zh: 命尚書左丞王宇副康王使斡離不軍，宇辭。

translations.literal: Left vice director Wang Yu was ordered to assist Prince Kang on embassy to Wolibu’s army; Yu declined.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Yu was ordered to assist Prince Kang to Wolibu’s army; Yu declined.

sentences.zh: 乙卯，雨木冰。

translations.literal: Day yimao: trees bore ice rain.
translations.idiomatic: On yimao, trees bore ice rain.

sentences.zh: 丙辰，金人陷平陽府，又陷威勝、隆德、澤州。

translations.literal: Day bingchen: the Jin took Pingyang prefecture and again took Weisheng, Longde, and Ze prefectures.
translations.idiomatic: On bingchen, the Jin took Pingyang and again took Weisheng, Longde, and Ze.

sentences.zh: 丁巳，高麗入貢，令明州遞表以進，遣其使還。

translations.literal: Day dingsi: Goryeo presented tribute; Mingzhou was ordered to relay the memorial for presentation, and its envoys were sent back.
translations.idiomatic: On dingsi, Goryeo presented tribute; Mingzhou relayed the memorial and sent the envoys back.

sentences.zh: 戊午，貶王宇為單州團練副使，命馮澥代行。

translations.literal: Day wuwu: Wang Yu was demoted to Shanzhou training vice commissioner; Feng Xu was ordered to go in his place.
translations.idiomatic: On wuwu, Wang Yu was demoted to Shanzhou training vice commissioner; Feng Xu went in his place.

sentences.zh: 庚申，日有兩珥及背氣。

translations.literal: Day gengshen: the sun had two ear-rings and back-glow.
translations.idiomatic: On gengshen, the sun had two ear-rings and back-glow.

sentences.zh: 侍御史胡舜陟請援中山，不省。

translations.literal: Attendant censor Hu Shunzhi requested relief for Zhongshan; it was not heeded.
translations.idiomatic: Attendant censor Hu Shunzhi requested relief for Zhongshan; it was not heeded.

sentences.zh: 辛酉，种師道薨。

translations.literal: Day xinyou: Zhong Shidao died.
translations.idiomatic: On xinyou, Zhong Shidao died.

sentences.zh: 十一月丙寅，夏人陷懷德軍，知軍事劉銓、通判杜翊世死之。

translations.literal: Eleventh month, day bingyin: the Xia took Huaide Army; military commissioner Liu Quan and prefectural judge Du Yishi died.
translations.idiomatic: Eleventh month, bingyin: the Xia took Huaide Army; Liu Quan and Du Yishi died.

sentences.zh: 籍譚稹家。

translations.literal: Tan Ji’s household goods were registered.
translations.idiomatic: Tan Ji’s household goods were registered.

sentences.zh: 戊辰，康王未至金軍而還。

translations.literal: Day wuchen: Prince Kang had not reached the Jin army when he returned.
translations.idiomatic: On wuchen, Prince Kang had not reached the Jin army when he returned.

sentences.zh: 馮澥罷。

translations.literal: Feng Xu was dismissed.
translations.idiomatic: Feng Xu was dismissed.

sentences.zh: 己巳，集百官議三鎮棄守。

translations.literal: Day jisi: all officials were assembled to deliberate abandoning and holding the three circuits.
translations.idiomatic: On jisi, all officials assembled to deliberate abandoning the three circuits.

sentences.zh: 庚午，詔河北、河東、京畿清野，令流民得占官舍寺觀以居。

translations.literal: Day gengwu: an edict ordered Hebei, Hedong, and the capital region cleared; refugees were permitted to occupy official lodges and temples to dwell.
translations.idiomatic: On gengwu, Hebei, Hedong, and the capital region were ordered cleared; refugees might occupy official lodges and temples.

sentences.zh: 辛未，有流星如杯。

translations.literal: Day xinwei: a meteor like a cup appeared.
translations.idiomatic: On xinwei, a cup-sized meteor appeared.

sentences.zh: 壬申，禁京師民以浮言相動者。

translations.literal: Day renshen: the capital’s people were forbidden to stir one another with loose talk.
translations.idiomatic: On renshen, the capital’s people were forbidden to stir one another with loose talk.

sentences.zh: 癸酉，右諫議大夫范宗尹以首議棄地罷。

translations.literal: Day guiyou: Right Remonstrance Bureau drafter Fan Zongyin was dismissed for first proposing to abandon territory.
translations.idiomatic: On guiyou, Fan Zongyin was dismissed for first proposing to abandon territory.

sentences.zh: 金人至河外，宣撫副使折彥質領師十二萬拒之。

translations.literal: The Jin reached beyond the Yellow River; deputy pacification commissioner Zhe Yanzi led one hundred twenty thousand troops to resist them.
translations.idiomatic: The Jin reached beyond the Yellow River; Zhe Yanzi led one hundred twenty thousand troops to resist.

sentences.zh: 甲戌，師潰。

translations.literal: Day jiaxu: the army collapsed.
translations.idiomatic: On jiaxu, the army collapsed.

sentences.zh: 金人濟河，知河陽燕瑛、西京留守王襄棄城遁。

translations.literal: The Jin crossed the river; Heyang prefect Yan Ying and Western Capital intendant Wang Xiang abandoned their cities and fled.
translations.idiomatic: The Jin crossed the river; Yan Ying and Wang Xiang abandoned their cities and fled.

sentences.zh: 乙亥，命刑部尚書王雲副康王使斡離不軍。

translations.literal: Day yihai: Minister of Punishments Wang Yun was ordered to assist Prince Kang on embassy to Wolibu’s army.
translations.idiomatic: On yihai, Wang Yun was ordered to assist Prince Kang to Wolibu’s army.

sentences.zh: 許割三鎮，奉袞冕、車輅，尊其主為皇叔，且上尊號。

translations.literal: Cession of the three circuits was permitted, with dragon robes and chariots presented, their ruler honored as imperial uncle, and an honorific title also offered.
translations.idiomatic: The three circuits might be ceded, with dragon robes and chariots presented, their ruler honored as imperial uncle, and an honorific offered.

sentences.zh: 丙子，金人渡河，折彥質兵盡潰，提刑許高兵潰於洛口。

translations.literal: Day bingzi: the Jin crossed the river; Zhe Yanzi’s troops wholly collapsed, and judicial commissioner Xu Gao’s troops collapsed at Luokou.
translations.idiomatic: On bingzi, the Jin crossed the river; Zhe Yanzi’s troops wholly collapsed and Xu Gao’s at Luokou.

sentences.zh: 金人來言，欲盡得河北地。

translations.literal: The Jin came saying they wished to take all Hebei territory.
translations.idiomatic: The Jin came saying they wished to take all Hebei.

sentences.zh: 京師戒嚴。

translations.literal: The capital was placed under martial law.
translations.idiomatic: The capital was placed under martial law.

sentences.zh: 遣資政殿學士馮澥及李若水使粘罕軍。

translations.literal: Academician of the Hall for Assisting Governance Feng Xu and Li Ruoshui were sent as envoys to Nianhan’s army.
translations.idiomatic: Feng Xu and Li Ruoshui were sent as envoys to Nianhan’s army.

sentences.zh: 丁丑，何㮚罢。

translations.literal: Day dingchou: He Xu was dismissed.
translations.idiomatic: On dingchou, He Xu was dismissed.

sentences.zh: 以尚書左丞陳過庭為中書侍郎，兵部尚書孫傅為尚書右丞。

translations.literal: Left vice director Chen Guoting was made vice director of the Secretariat; Minister of War Sun Fu was made right vice director.
translations.idiomatic: Chen Guoting became Secretariat vice director; Sun Fu became right vice director.

sentences.zh: 命成忠郎郭京領選六甲正兵所。

translations.literal: Loyal Merit Gentleman Guo Jing was ordered to lead the selected Six Jia regular troops office.
translations.idiomatic: Loyal Merit Gentleman Guo Jing was ordered to lead the selected Six Jia regular troops.

sentences.zh: 簽書樞密院事李回以萬騎防河，眾潰而歸。

translations.literal: Signing secretary of the Bureau of Military Affairs Li Hui, with ten thousand horsemen to defend the river, had the host collapse and return.
translations.idiomatic: Li Hui, with ten thousand horsemen to defend the river, had the host collapse and return.

sentences.zh: 是日，塞京城門。

translations.literal: That day the capital’s gates were blocked.
translations.idiomatic: That day the capital’s gates were blocked.

sentences.zh: 戊寅，進龍德宮婉容韋氏為賢妃，康王構為安國、安武軍節度使。

translations.literal: Day wuyin: Longde Palace’s Graceful Consort Wei was advanced to Worthy Consort; Prince Kang Gou was made An’guo and Anwu military commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: On wuyin, Consort Wei was advanced to Worthy Consort; Prince Kang Gou became An’guo and Anwu military commissioner.

sentences.zh: 罷清野。

translations.literal: The order to clear the countryside was revoked.
translations.idiomatic: The order to clear the countryside was revoked.

sentences.zh: 辛巳，以知懷州霍安國為徽猷閣待制，通判林淵直徽猷閣，賞守禦之功也。

translations.literal: Day xinsi: Huai prefecture prefect Huo Anguo was made Palace Attendant; prefectural judge Lin Yuan was made direct Palace Attendant, rewarding merit in defense.
translations.idiomatic: On xinsi, Huo Anguo became Palace Attendant and Lin Yuan direct Palace Attendant, rewarding defensive merit.

sentences.zh: 壬午，斡離不使楊天吉、王汭、勃堇撒離栂來。

translations.literal: Day renwu: Wolibu sent Yang Tiangi, Wang Rui, and Bojin Salimai.
translations.idiomatic: On renwu, Wolibu sent Yang Tiangi, Wang Rui, and Bojin Salimai.

sentences.zh: 命耿南仲使斡離不軍，聶昌使粘罕軍，許畫河為界。

translations.literal: Geng Nanzhong was ordered to Wolibu’s army, Nie Chang to Nianhan’s army, with the Yellow River drawn as boundary permitted.
translations.idiomatic: Geng Nanzhong was sent to Wolibu’s army and Nie Chang to Nianhan’s, with the Yellow River as boundary permitted.

sentences.zh: 康王至磁州，州人殺王雲，止王勿行，王復還相州。

translations.literal: Prince Kang reached Cizhou; the people killed Wang Yun and stopped the prince from going; the prince returned again to Xiangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Kang reached Cizhou; the people killed Wang Yun and stopped him from going; the prince returned to Xiangzhou.

sentences.zh: 甲申，以尚書右丞孫傅同知樞密院事，御史中丞曹輔簽書樞密院事。

translations.literal: Day jiashen: right vice director Sun Fu was made associate director of the Bureau of Military Affairs; chief censor Cao Fu signing secretary.
translations.idiomatic: On jiashen, Sun Fu became associate military affairs director and Cao Fu signing secretary.

sentences.zh: 以京兆府路安撫使范致虛為陝西五路宣撫使，令督勤王兵入援。

translations.literal: Jingzhao circuit pacification commissioner Fan Zhixu was made Shaanxi five-circuit pacification commissioner, ordered to urge relief armies of loyal princes to enter and aid.
translations.idiomatic: Fan Zhixu became Shaanxi five-circuit pacification commissioner, ordered to urge loyalist armies to aid.

sentences.zh: 乙酉，斡離不軍至城下。

translations.literal: Day yiyou: Wolibu’s army reached below the walls.
translations.idiomatic: On yiyou, Wolibu’s army reached below the walls.

sentences.zh: 遣蠟書間行出關召兵，又約康王及河北守將來援。

translations.literal: Wax-sealed letters were sent by secret routes out of the passes to summon troops; it was also arranged that Prince Kang and Hebei garrison commanders should come to aid.
translations.idiomatic: Wax-sealed letters went out by secret routes to summon troops; Prince Kang and Hebei commanders were also to aid.

sentences.zh: 多為邏兵所獲。

translations.literal: Many were captured by border troops.
translations.idiomatic: Many were captured by border troops.

sentences.zh: 丁亥，大風髮屋折木。

translations.literal: Day dinghai: great wind tore off roofs and broke trees.
translations.idiomatic: On dinghai, great wind tore off roofs and broke trees.

sentences.zh: 李回罷。

translations.literal: Li Hui was dismissed.
translations.idiomatic: Li Hui was dismissed.

sentences.zh: 戊子，金人攻通津門，范瓊出兵焚其砦。

translations.literal: Day wuzi: the Jin attacked Tongjin Gate; Fan Qiong led troops out and burned their stockade.
translations.idiomatic: On wuzi, the Jin attacked Tongjin Gate; Fan Qiong led troops out and burned their stockade.

sentences.zh: 己丑，南道總管張叔夜將兵勤王，至玉津園，以叔夜為延康殿學士。

translations.literal: Day jichou: south-circuit grand marshal Zhang Shuye led troops in loyal service to the throne and reached Yujin Garden; Shuye was made Academician of the Hall for Assisting Governance.
translations.idiomatic: On jichou, Zhang Shuye led loyalist troops to Yujin Garden and was made Academician of the Hall for Assisting Governance.

sentences.zh: 斡離不遣劉晏來。

translations.literal: Wolibu sent Liu Yan.
translations.idiomatic: Wolibu sent Liu Yan.

sentences.zh: 庚寅，幸東壁勞軍。

translations.literal: Day gengyin: the emperor went to the eastern wall to encourage the army.
translations.idiomatic: On gengyin, the emperor went to the eastern wall to encourage the army.

sentences.zh: 詔三省長官名悉依元豐舊制。

translations.literal: An edict: the chief ministers’ titles in the Three Departments should all follow the Yuanfeng old system.
translations.idiomatic: The Three Departments’ chief titles were ordered to follow the Yuanfeng old system.

sentences.zh: 領開封府何㮚為門下侍郎。

translations.literal: He Xu, holding Kaifeng prefecture, was made vice director of the Chancellery.
translations.idiomatic: He Xu, holding Kaifeng, became Chancellery vice director.

sentences.zh: 閏月壬辰朔，金人攻善利門，統制姚仲友禦之。

translations.literal: Intercalary month, day renchen new moon: the Jin attacked Shanli Gate; controller Yao Zhongyou defended it.
translations.idiomatic: Intercalary month, renchen new moon: the Jin attacked Shanli Gate; Yao Zhongyou defended it.

sentences.zh: 奇兵作亂，殺使臣，王宗濋斬數十人乃定。

translations.literal: Strange troops mutinied and killed envoys; Wang Zongyin executed several tens of men before order was restored.
translations.idiomatic: Strange troops mutinied and killed envoys; Wang Zongyin executed several tens before order was restored.

sentences.zh: 唐恪出都，人欲擊之，因求去，罷為中太一宮使。

translations.literal: Tang Que left the capital; the people wished to strike him, so he begged to go and was dismissed as superintendent of the Central Grand Unity Abbey.
translations.idiomatic: Tang Que left the capital; the people wished to strike him, so he begged to go and was dismissed as Central Grand Unity superintendent.

sentences.zh: 以門下侍郎何㮚為尚書右僕射兼中書侍郎。

translations.literal: Chancellery vice director He Xu was made right vice director of the Department of State Affairs and concurrently vice director of the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: He Xu became right vice director and concurrently Secretariat vice director.

sentences.zh: 劉韐坐棄軍，降五官予祠。

translations.literal: Liu Ge, guilty of abandoning the army, was demoted five grades and given a sinecure.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Ge was demoted five grades and given a sinecure for abandoning the army.

sentences.zh: 癸巳，京師苦寒，用日者言，借土牛迎春。

translations.literal: Day guisi: the capital was bitterly cold; following the day-officials’ advice, an earth ox was borrowed to welcome spring.
translations.idiomatic: On guisi, the capital was bitterly cold; following day-officials’ advice, an earth ox was borrowed to welcome spring.

sentences.zh: 朱伯友坐棄鄭州，降三官罷。

translations.literal: Zhu Boyou, guilty of abandoning Zhengzhou, was demoted three grades and dismissed.
translations.idiomatic: Zhu Boyou was demoted three grades and dismissed for abandoning Zhengzhou.

sentences.zh: 西道總管王襄棄西京去。

translations.literal: West-circuit grand marshal Wang Xiang abandoned the Western Capital and left.
translations.idiomatic: West-circuit grand marshal Wang Xiang abandoned the Western Capital and left.

sentences.zh: 知澤州高世由以城降于金。

translations.literal: Ze prefecture prefect Gao Shiyou surrendered the city to the Jin.
translations.idiomatic: Ze prefect Gao Shiyou surrendered the city to the Jin.

sentences.zh: 燕瑛欲棄河陽，為亂兵所殺。

translations.literal: Yan Ying wished to abandon Heyang but was killed by mutinous troops.
translations.idiomatic: Yan Ying wished to abandon Heyang but was killed by mutinous troops.

sentences.zh: 河東諸郡，或降或破殆盡。

translations.literal: Hedong’s prefectures and commanderies were nearly all surrendered or taken.
translations.idiomatic: Hedong’s prefectures and commanderies were nearly all surrendered or taken.

sentences.zh: 都民殺東壁統制官辛亢宗。

translations.literal: The capital’s people killed eastern-wall controller Xin Kangzong.
translations.idiomatic: The capital’s people killed eastern-wall controller Xin Kangzong.

sentences.zh: 罷民乘城，代以保甲。

translations.literal: The people were dismissed from manning the walls; security groups replaced them.
translations.idiomatic: The people were dismissed from the walls; security groups replaced them.

sentences.zh: 粘罕軍至城下。

translations.literal: Nianhan’s army reached below the walls.
translations.idiomatic: Nianhan’s army reached below the walls.

sentences.zh: 甲午，時雨雪交作，帝被甲登城，以禦膳賜士卒，易火飯以進，人皆感激流涕。

translations.literal: Day jiawu: as snow and rain fell together, the emperor donned armor and ascended the wall, bestowing imperial meals on the soldiers and exchanging hot rice to serve them; all were moved to grateful tears.
translations.idiomatic: On jiawu, as snow and rain fell, the emperor donned armor, ascended the wall, bestowed imperial meals, and served hot rice; all wept in gratitude.

sentences.zh: 金人攻通津門，數百人縋城禦之，焚其炮架五、鵝車二。

translations.literal: The Jin attacked Tongjin Gate; several hundred men were lowered by rope from the wall to defend; five catapult frames and two goose carts were burned.
translations.idiomatic: The Jin attacked Tongjin Gate; several hundred men were lowered by rope to defend; five catapults and two goose carts were burned.

sentences.zh: 驛召李綱為資政殿大學士、領開封府。

translations.literal: By urgent dispatch Li Gang was made Grand Academician of the Hall for Assisting Governance and given charge of Kaifeng prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Li Gang was urgently made Grand Academician and given Kaifeng prefecture.

sentences.zh: 金人陷懷州，霍安國、林淵及其鈐轄張彭年、都監趙士詝、張諶皆死之。

translations.literal: The Jin took Huai prefecture; Huo Anguo, Lin Yuan, and their commanders Zhang Pengnian, overseer Zhao Shizhuo, and Zhang Chen all died.
translations.idiomatic: The Jin took Huai; Huo Anguo, Lin Yuan, Zhang Pengnian, Zhao Shizhuo, and Zhang Chen all died.

sentences.zh: 乙未，金人入青城，攻朝陽門。

translations.literal: Day yiwei: the Jin entered the Greenwall suburb and attacked Chaoyang Gate.
translations.idiomatic: On yiwei, the Jin entered the Greenwall suburb and attacked Chaoyang Gate.

sentences.zh: 馮澥與金人蕭慶、楊真誥來。

translations.literal: Feng Xu came with the Jin men Xiao Qing and Yang Zhengao.
translations.idiomatic: Feng Xu came with the Jin men Xiao Qing and Yang Zhengao.

sentences.zh: 丙申，帝幸宣化門，以障泥乘馬，行泥淖中，民皆感泣。

translations.literal: Day bingshen: the emperor went to Xu Gate, riding a horse with mud-guards through the mire; the people all wept.
translations.idiomatic: On bingshen, the emperor went to Xu Gate, riding through the mire with mud-guards; the people wept.

sentences.zh: 張叔夜數戰有功，帝如安上門召見，拜資政殿學士。

translations.literal: Zhang Shuye fought several times with merit; the emperor went to An Gate to summon him and made him Academician of the Hall for Assisting Governance.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Shuye fought several times with merit; the emperor summoned him at An Gate and made him Academician of the Hall for Assisting Governance.

sentences.zh: 金人執胡直孺，又陷拱州。

translations.literal: The Jin seized Hu Zhiru and again took Gong prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: The Jin seized Hu Zhiru and again took Gong prefecture.

sentences.zh: 丁酉，赤氣亙天。

translations.literal: Day dingyou: red vapor stretched across heaven.
translations.idiomatic: On dingyou, red vapor stretched across heaven.

sentences.zh: 以馮澥為尚書左丞。

translations.literal: Feng Xu was made left vice director of the Department of State Affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Feng Xu was made left vice director.

sentences.zh: 戊戌，殿前副都指揮使王宗濋與金人戰於城下，統制官高師旦死之。

translations.literal: Day wuxu: Hall front deputy commander Wang Zongyin fought the Jin below the wall; controller Gao Shidan died.
translations.idiomatic: On wuxu, Wang Zongyin fought the Jin below the wall; Gao Shidan died.

sentences.zh: 庚子，以資政殿學士張叔夜簽書樞密院事。

translations.literal: Day gengzi: Academician of the Hall for Assisting Governance Zhang Shuye was made signing secretary of the Bureau of Military Affairs.
translations.idiomatic: On gengzi, Zhang Shuye was made signing military affairs secretary.

sentences.zh: 金人攻宣化門，姚仲友禦之。

translations.literal: The Jin attacked Xu Gate; Yao Zhongyou defended it.
translations.idiomatic: The Jin attacked Xu Gate; Yao Zhongyou defended it.

sentences.zh: 辛丑，金人攻南壁，殺傷相當。

translations.literal: Day xinchou: the Jin attacked the southern wall; casualties were about equal.
translations.idiomatic: On xinchou, the Jin attacked the southern wall; casualties were about equal.

sentences.zh: 壬寅，詔河北守臣盡起軍民兵，倍道入援。

translations.literal: Day renyin: an edict ordered Hebei garrison officials to raise all militia and regular troops and enter aid by forced marches.
translations.idiomatic: On renyin, Hebei garrison officials were ordered to raise all troops and enter aid by forced marches.

sentences.zh: 癸卯，金人攻南壁，張叔夜、范瓊分兵襲之，遙見金兵，奔還，自相蹈藉，溺隍死者以千數。

translations.literal: Day guimao: the Jin attacked the southern wall; Zhang Shuye and Fan Qiong divided troops to raid them; from afar they saw Jin troops and ran back, trampling one another; those drowned in the moat numbered in the thousands.
translations.idiomatic: On guimao, the Jin attacked the southern wall; Zhang Shuye and Fan Qiong raided but fled at sight of Jin troops, trampling one another; thousands drowned in the moat.

sentences.zh: 甲辰，大雨雪。

translations.literal: Day jiachen: great rain and snow.
translations.idiomatic: On jiachen, great rain and snow fell.

sentences.zh: 金人陷亳州。

translations.literal: The Jin took Bozhou.
translations.idiomatic: The Jin took Bozhou.

sentences.zh: 遣間使召諸道兵勤王。

translations.literal: Secret envoys were sent to summon loyalist armies from every circuit.
translations.idiomatic: Secret envoys were sent to summon loyalist armies from every circuit.

sentences.zh: 乙巳，大寒，士卒噤戰不能執兵，有僵僕者。

translations.literal: Day yisi: bitter cold; soldiers shivered and could not grasp weapons; some stiffened and fell.
translations.idiomatic: On yisi, bitter cold left soldiers shivering and unable to grasp weapons; some stiffened and fell.

sentences.zh: 帝在禁中徒跣祈晴。

translations.literal: The emperor, in the inner palace, went barefoot to pray for clear weather.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor went barefoot in the inner palace to pray for clear weather.

sentences.zh: 時勤王兵不至，城中兵可用者惟衛士三萬，然亦十失五六。

translations.literal: At the time loyalist armies had not arrived; usable troops in the city were only thirty thousand guardsmen, and even of these five or six in ten were lost.
translations.idiomatic: Loyalist armies had not arrived; only thirty thousand guardsmen were usable, and even of these five or six in ten were lost.

sentences.zh: 金人攻城急。

translations.literal: The Jin pressed the assault on the city.
translations.idiomatic: The Jin pressed the assault on the city.

sentences.zh: 丙午，雨木冰。

translations.literal: Day bingwu: trees bore ice rain.
translations.idiomatic: On bingwu, trees bore ice rain.

sentences.zh: 丁未，始避正殿。

translations.literal: Day dingwei: the emperor at last left the main hall.
translations.idiomatic: On dingwei, the emperor at last left the main hall.

sentences.zh: 己酉，遣馮澥、曹輔與宗室仲溫、士訁布使金軍請和。

translations.literal: Day jiyou: Feng Xu, Cao Fu, and clansmen Zhongwen and Shishen were sent as envoys to the Jin army to beg peace.
translations.idiomatic: On jiyou, Feng Xu, Cao Fu, and clansmen Zhongwen and Shishen were sent to the Jin army to beg peace.

sentences.zh: 命康王為天下兵馬大元帥，速領兵入衛。

translations.literal: Prince Kang was made Grand Marshal of All Forces Under Heaven, urgently ordered to lead troops to enter and guard.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Kang was made Grand Marshal of All Forces Under Heaven, urgently ordered to lead troops to guard the throne.

sentences.zh: 辛亥，金人來議和，要親王出盟。

translations.literal: Day xinhai: the Jin came to discuss peace, demanding that a prince go out to covenant.
translations.idiomatic: On xinhai, the Jin came to discuss peace, demanding a prince go out to covenant.

sentences.zh: 壬子，金人攻通津、宣化門，范瓊以千人出戰，渡河，冰裂，沒者五百餘人，自是士氣益挫。

translations.literal: Day renzi: the Jin attacked Tongjin and Xu gates; Fan Qiong led a thousand men out to fight; crossing the river, the ice broke and more than five hundred were drowned; from then morale was further broken.
translations.idiomatic: On renzi, the Jin attacked Tongjin and Xu gates; Fan Qiong led a thousand out; crossing the river the ice broke and more than five hundred drowned; morale broke further.

sentences.zh: 甲寅，大風自北起，俄大雨雪，連日夜不止。

translations.literal: Day jiayin: great wind rose from the north; soon great rain and snow fell, continuing day and night without cease.
translations.idiomatic: On jiayin, great wind rose from the north; soon rain and snow fell day and night without cease.

sentences.zh: 乙卯，金人復使劉晏來，趣親王、宰相出盟。

translations.literal: Day yimao: the Jin again sent Liu Yan, urging a prince and the chief minister to go out to covenant.
translations.idiomatic: On yimao, the Jin again sent Liu Yan, urging a prince and chief minister to covenant.

sentences.zh: 丙辰，妖人郭京用六甲法，盡令守禦人下城，大啟宣化門出攻金人，兵大敗。

translations.literal: Day bingchen: the charlatan Guo Jing used the Six Jia method, ordering all defenders off the wall, widely opening Xu Gate to sally against the Jin; the army was greatly defeated.
translations.idiomatic: On bingchen, charlatan Guo Jing used the Six Jia method, ordered defenders off the wall, opened Xu Gate wide to sally, and was greatly defeated.

sentences.zh: 京托言下城作法，引餘兵遁去。

translations.literal: Jing pretended to descend the wall to perform the rite and led the remaining troops in flight.
translations.idiomatic: Jing pretended to descend the wall to perform the rite and led the remaining troops in flight.

sentences.zh: 金兵登城，眾皆披靡。

translations.literal: Jin soldiers ascended the wall; the host all collapsed.
translations.idiomatic: Jin soldiers ascended the wall; the host all collapsed.

sentences.zh: 金人焚南薰諸門。

translations.literal: The Jin burned the southern Xun and other gates.
translations.idiomatic: The Jin burned the southern Xun and other gates.

sentences.zh: 姚仲友死于亂兵，宦者黃經國赴火死，統制官何慶言、陳克禮、中書舍人高振力戰，與其家人皆被害。

translations.literal: Yao Zhongyou died among mutinous troops; eunuch Huang Jingguo threw himself into fire and died; controllers He Qingyan and Chen Keli and drafting attendant Gao Zhen fought stoutly and, with their families, were all killed.
translations.idiomatic: Yao Zhongyou died among mutinous troops; Huang Jingguo burned himself; He Qingyan, Chen Keli, and Gao Zhen fought stoutly and, with their families, were all killed.

sentences.zh: 秦元領保甲斬關遁，京城陷。

translations.literal: Qin Yuan led security groups to cut the passes and flee; the capital fell.
translations.idiomatic: Qin Yuan led security groups to cut the passes and flee; the capital fell.

sentences.zh: 衛士入都亭驛，執劉晏，殺之。

translations.literal: Guardsmen entered the Capital Pavilion and seized Liu Yan and killed him.
translations.idiomatic: Guardsmen entered the Capital Pavilion, seized Liu Yan, and killed him.

sentences.zh: 丁巳，奉道君皇帝、甯德皇后入居延福宮。

translations.literal: Day dingsi: the Retired Emperor and Ningde Empress were moved to dwell at Yanfu Palace.
translations.idiomatic: On dingsi, the Retired Emperor and Ningde Empress moved to Yanfu Palace.

sentences.zh: 命何㮚及済王栩使金軍。

translations.literal: He Xu and Prince Ji Xu were ordered as envoys to the Jin army.
translations.idiomatic: He Xu and Prince Ji Xu were ordered as envoys to the Jin army.

sentences.zh: 戊午，何㮚入言，金人邀上皇出郊。

translations.literal: Day wuwu: He Xu entered and reported that the Jin invited the Retired Emperor to go out to the suburbs.
translations.idiomatic: On wuwu, He Xu reported that the Jin invited the Retired Emperor to the suburbs.

sentences.zh: 帝曰：「上皇驚憂而疾，必欲之出，朕當親往。

translations.literal: The emperor said: “The Retired Emperor is alarmed and ill; if he must go out, I shall go in person.”
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said: “The Retired Emperor is alarmed and ill; if he must go out, I shall go in person.”

sentences.zh: 」自乙卯雪不止，是日霽。

translations.literal: From yimao snow had not ceased; that day it cleared.
translations.idiomatic: From yimao snow had not ceased; that day it cleared.

sentences.zh: 夜有白氣出太微，彗星見。

translations.literal: By night white vapor issued from Supreme Subtlety; a comet appeared.
translations.idiomatic: By night white vapor issued from Supreme Subtlety; a comet appeared.

sentences.zh: 庚申，日赤如火，無光。

translations.literal: Day gengshen: the sun was red as fire and without light.
translations.idiomatic: On gengshen, the sun was red as fire and without light.

sentences.zh: 辛酉，帝如青城。

translations.literal: Day xinyou: the emperor went to the Greenwall suburb.
translations.idiomatic: On xinyou, the emperor went to the Greenwall suburb.

sentences.zh: 十二月壬戌朔，帝在青城。

translations.literal: Twelfth month, day renxu new moon: the emperor was at the Greenwall suburb.
translations.idiomatic: Twelfth month, renxu new moon: the emperor was at the Greenwall suburb.

sentences.zh: 蕭慶入居尚書省。

translations.literal: Xiao Qing moved into the Department of State Affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Xiao Qing took up residence in the Department of State Affairs.

sentences.zh: 是日，康王開大元帥府于相州。

translations.literal: That day, Kang Wang opened the Great Marshal’s Headquarters at Xiangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: That day Kang Wang opened the Great Marshal’s Headquarters at Xiangzhou.

sentences.zh: 癸亥，帝至自青城。

translations.literal: Day guihai: the emperor returned from Qingcheng.
translations.idiomatic: On guihai, the emperor returned from Qingcheng.

sentences.zh: 甲子，大索金帛。

translations.literal: Day jiazi: a great search for gold and silk was made.
translations.idiomatic: On jiazi, gold and silk were seized throughout the city.

sentences.zh: 丙寅，遣陳過庭、劉韐使兩河割地。

translations.literal: Day bingyin: Chen Guoting and Liu Lin were sent as envoys to cede lands in the Two He circuits.
translations.idiomatic: On bingyin, Chen Guoting and Liu Lin were sent to cede the Two He circuits.

sentences.zh: 辛未，定京師米價，勸糶以振民。

translations.literal: Day xinwei: capital grain prices were fixed and state sales were urged to relieve the people.
translations.idiomatic: On xinwei, capital grain prices were fixed and government grain was sold cheap to aid the people.

sentences.zh: 癸酉，斬行門指揮使蔣宣、李福。

translations.literal: Day guiyou: gate-guard commanders Jiang Xuan and Li Fu were executed.
translations.idiomatic: On guiyou, gate-guard commanders Jiang Xuan and Li Fu were beheaded.

sentences.zh: 乙亥，康王如北京。

translations.literal: Day yihai: Kang Wang went to Beijing.
translations.idiomatic: On yihai, Kang Wang went to Beijing.

sentences.zh: 丙子，尚書省火。

translations.literal: Day bingzi: the Department of State Affairs caught fire.
translations.idiomatic: On bingzi, the Department of State Affairs burned.

sentences.zh: 庚辰，雨雹。

translations.literal: Day gengchen: hail fell.
translations.idiomatic: On gengchen, hail fell.

sentences.zh: 癸未，大雪，寒。

translations.literal: Day guiwei: heavy snow fell and it was bitterly cold.
translations.idiomatic: On guiwei, heavy snow fell in bitter cold.

sentences.zh: 縱民伐紫筠館花木為薪。

translations.literal: The people were allowed to cut the flowers and trees of the Purple Bamboo Pavilion for firewood.
translations.idiomatic: Commoners were allowed to cut Purple Bamboo Pavilion trees for fuel.

sentences.zh: 庚寅，康王如東平。

translations.literal: Day gengyin: Kang Wang went to Dongping.
translations.idiomatic: On gengyin, Kang Wang went to Dongping.

sentences.zh: 二年春正月辛卯朔，命濟王栩、景王杞出賀金軍，金人亦遣使入賀。

translations.literal: Jingkang year 2, spring, first month, day xinmao new moon: the Prince of Ji, Xu, and the Prince of Jing, Qi, were ordered out to congratulate the Jin army; the Jin also sent envoys in to congratulate.
translations.idiomatic: Jingkang 2, spring, xinmao new moon: Princes Xu of Ji and Qi of Jing were sent to congratulate the Jin army, which also sent envoys to congratulate in turn.

sentences.zh: 壬辰，金人趣召康王還。

translations.literal: Day renchen: the Jin urgently summoned Kang Wang back.
translations.idiomatic: On renchen, Jin urgently recalled Kang Wang.

sentences.zh: 遣聶昌、耿南仲、陳過庭出割兩河地，民堅守不奉詔，凡累月，止得石州。

translations.literal: Nie Chang, Geng Nanzhong, and Chen Guoting were sent to cede the Two He lands; the people held firm and would not obey the edict—for many months in all they obtained only Shizhou.
translations.idiomatic: Nie Chang, Geng Nanzhong, and Chen Guoting went to cede the Two He circuits, but the people refused the edict; after months they secured only Shizhou.

sentences.zh: 甲午，詔兩河民開門出降。

translations.literal: Day wuwu: an edict ordered the people of the Two He circuits to open their gates and surrender.
translations.idiomatic: On wuwu, an edict ordered the Two He circuits to open their gates and submit.

sentences.zh: 乙未，有大星出建星，西南流入於濁沒。

translations.literal: Day weijing: a great star appeared at Jianxing and flowed southwest into Zhuomo.
translations.idiomatic: On weijing, a great star rose at Jianxing and swept southwest into Zhuomo.

sentences.zh: 丁酉，雨木冰。

translations.literal: Day dingyou: trees were coated with ice from rain.
translations.idiomatic: On dingyou, freezing rain glazed the trees.

sentences.zh: 己亥，陰曀，風迅發。

translations.literal: Day jihai: the sky was overcast and dim.
translations.idiomatic: On jihai, the sky hung dark and dim.

sentences.zh: 夜，西北陰雲中有如火光。

translations.literal: At night, in the northwest within dark clouds there was something like firelight.
translations.idiomatic: That night firelike light shone in the northwestern clouds.

sentences.zh: 庚子，金人索金銀急。

translations.literal: Day gengzi: the Jin urgently demanded gold and silver.
translations.idiomatic: On gengzi, Jin urgently demanded gold and silver.

sentences.zh: 何㮚、李若水勸帝親至軍中，從之，以太子監國而行。

translations.literal: He Li and Li Ruoshui urged the emperor to go to the army in person; he followed their advice, leaving the crown prince to supervise the state while he went.
translations.idiomatic: He Li and Li Ruoshui urged Qinzong to go to the Jin camp in person; he agreed, leaving the crown prince as regent.

sentences.zh: 乙巳，籍梁師成家。

translations.literal: Day yisi: Liang Shicheng’s household property was registered for confiscation.
translations.idiomatic: On yisi, Liang Shicheng’s property was seized.

sentences.zh: 丙午，劉韐自經于金軍。

translations.literal: Day bingwu: Liu Lin hanged himself in the Jin camp.
translations.idiomatic: On bingwu, Liu Lin hanged himself in the Jin camp.

sentences.zh: 太學生徐揆上書，乞守門請帝還闕。

translations.literal: Imperial University student Xu Kui submitted a memorial begging to guard the gate and ask that the emperor return to the palace.
translations.idiomatic: Imperial University student Xu Kui memorialized, begging to guard the gate and plead for the emperor’s return to the palace.

sentences.zh: 金人取至軍中，揆抗論，為所殺。

translations.literal: The Jin took him to their camp; Kui argued defiantly and was killed by them.
translations.idiomatic: Jin seized him to their camp; Kui remonstrated boldly and was killed.

sentences.zh: 至夜，金人劫神衛營。

translations.literal: At night the Jin raided the Divine Guard camp.
translations.idiomatic: That night Jin raided the Divine Guard camp.

sentences.zh: 丁未，大霧四塞。

translations.literal: Day dingwei: heavy fog filled the four quarters.
translations.idiomatic: On dingwei, heavy fog closed in on every side.

sentences.zh: 金人下含輝門剽掠，焚五嶽觀。

translations.literal: The Jin came down through Hanhui Gate to plunder and burned the Five Sacred Peaks Abbey.
translations.idiomatic: Jin poured through Hanhui Gate to loot and burned the Five Sacred Peaks Abbey.

sentences.zh: 二月辛酉朔，帝在青城，自如金軍，都人出迎賀。

translations.literal: Second month, day xinmao new moon: the emperor was at Qingcheng; he came from the Jin army himself, and the people of the capital came out to welcome and congratulate.
translations.idiomatic: Second month, xinmao new moon: at Qingcheng the emperor returned from the Jin camp himself, and the capital crowd came out to welcome him.

sentences.zh: 丙寅，金人塹南薰門路，人心大恐。

translations.literal: Day bingyin: the Jin trenched the road at Nanxun Gate, and hearts in the capital were greatly terrified.
translations.idiomatic: On bingyin, Jin dug trenches across Nanxun Gate road, and terror seized the city.

sentences.zh: 已而金人令推立異姓，孫傅方號慟，乞立趙氏，不允。

translations.literal: Soon the Jin ordered that a man of another surname be set up; Sun Fu was then wailing aloud, begging that a Zhao be enthroned, but it was not granted.
translations.idiomatic: Soon Jin demanded a non-Zhao ruler; Sun Fu wailed and begged for a Zhao emperor, but they refused.

sentences.zh: 丁卯，金人要上皇如青城。

translations.literal: Day dingmao: the Jin wanted the Retired Emperor to go to Qingcheng.
translations.idiomatic: On dingmao, Jin required Huizong to go to Qingcheng.

sentences.zh: 以內侍鄧述所具諸王孫名，盡取入軍中。

translations.literal: On the list of imperial grandsons’ names furnished by palace attendant Deng Shu, all were taken into the Jin camp.
translations.idiomatic: From palace attendant Deng Shu’s roll of imperial grandsons, every name was taken into the Jin camp.

sentences.zh: 辛未，金人逼上皇召皇后、皇太子入青城。

translations.literal: Day xinwei: the Jin forced the Retired Emperor to summon the empress and crown prince to Qingcheng.
translations.idiomatic: On xinwei, Jin forced Huizong to summon the empress and crown prince to Qingcheng.

sentences.zh: 庚辰，康王如濟州。

translations.literal: Day gengchen: Kang Wang went to Jizhou.
translations.idiomatic: On gengchen, Kang Wang went to Jizhou.

sentences.zh: 癸未，觀文殿大學士唐恪仰藥自殺。

translations.literal: Day guiwei: Scholar of the Hall of Assembled Literature Tang Que took poison and killed himself.
translations.idiomatic: On guiwei, Tang Que, scholar of the Hall of Assembled Literature, took poison and died.

sentences.zh: 乙酉，金人以括金未足，殺戶部尚書梅執禮、侍郎陳知質、刑部侍郎程振、給事中安扶。

translations.literal: Day yiyou: because the gold levy was still short, Revenue Minister Mei Zhili, Vice Minister Chen Zhizhi, Punishments Vice Minister Cheng Zhen, and Secretariat Drafter An Fu were killed.
translations.idiomatic: On yiyou, with the gold levy still short, Mei Zhili, Chen Zhizhi, Cheng Zhen, and An Fu were executed.

sentences.zh: 三月辛卯朔，帝在青城。

translations.literal: Third month, day xinmao new moon: the emperor was at Qingcheng.
translations.idiomatic: Third month, xinmao new moon: the emperor remained at Qingcheng.

sentences.zh: 丁酉，金人立張邦昌為楚帝。

translations.literal: Day dingyou: the Jin enthroned Zhang Bangchang as Emperor of Chu.
translations.idiomatic: On dingyou, Jin set up Zhang Bangchang as Emperor of Chu.

sentences.zh: 庚子，金人來取宗室，開封尹徐秉哲令民結保，毋藏匿。

translations.literal: Day gengzi: the Jin came to take the imperial clan; Kaifeng magistrate Xu Bingzhe ordered mutual-responsibility groups and forbade concealment.
translations.idiomatic: On gengzi, Jin came for the imperial clan; Kaifeng magistrate Xu Bingzhe ordered neighborhood groups and forbade hiding anyone.

sentences.zh: 丁巳，金人脅上皇北行。

translations.literal: Day dingsi: the Jin coerced the Retired Emperor to travel north.
translations.idiomatic: On dingsi, Jin drove Huizong north.

sentences.zh: 夏四月庚申朔，大風吹石折木。

translations.literal: Summer, fourth month, day gengshen new moon: a great wind blew stones and broke trees.
translations.idiomatic: Summer, fourth month, gengshen new moon: a gale hurled stones and snapped trees.

sentences.zh: 金人以帝及皇后、皇太子北歸。

translations.literal: The Jin took the emperor, the empress, and the crown prince back north.
translations.idiomatic: Jin marched the emperor, empress, and crown prince north.

sentences.zh: 凡法駕、鹵簿，皇后以下車輅、鹵簿，冠服、禮器、法物，大樂、教坊樂器，祭器、八寶、九鼎、圭璧，渾天儀、銅人、刻漏，古器、景靈宮供器，太清樓秘閣三館書、天下州府圖及官吏、內人、內侍、技藝、工匠、娼優，府庫畜積，為之一空。

translations.literal: Imperial equipage and guards of honor; below the empress, carriages and guards of honor; robes, caps, ritual vessels, and regalia; great music and Bureau of Music instruments; sacrificial vessels, the Eight Treasures, the Nine Tripods, jade disks and scepters; the armillary sphere, bronze man, and clepsydra; antiquities and Jingling Palace offerings; books of the Taiping Tower Secret Vault and Three Institutes, maps of all prefectures in the realm, officials, palace women, eunuchs, artisans, craftsmen, and courtesans; and treasury stores—all were swept utterly empty.
translations.idiomatic: Imperial carriages and guards of honor, the queen’s train, robes and ritual gear, court music and Bureau instruments, sacrificial vessels, the Eight Treasures and Nine Tripods, jades, the armillary sphere, bronze man, and clepsydra, antiquities, Jingling offerings, Taiping Tower and Three Institutes books, empire-wide maps, officials, palace women, eunuchs, artisans, craftsmen, courtesans, and treasury hoards—all were stripped away.

sentences.zh: 辛酉，北風大起，苦寒。

translations.literal: Day xinyou: the north wind rose greatly and it was bitterly cold.
translations.idiomatic: On xinyou, a fierce north wind brought bitter cold.

sentences.zh: 五月庚寅朔，康王即位于南京，遙上尊號曰孝慈淵聖皇帝。

translations.literal: Fifth month, day gengyin new moon: Kang Wang took the throne at the Southern Capital and remotely offered the honorific title Filial, Benevolent, Profound, and Sagely Emperor.
translations.idiomatic: Fifth month, gengyin new moon: Kang Wang ascended at the Southern Capital and offered Qinzong the remote title Filial, Benevolent, Profound, and Sagely Emperor.

sentences.zh: 紹興三十一年五月辛卯，帝崩問至。

translations.literal: Shaoxing year 31, fifth month, day xinmao: news of the emperor’s death arrived.
translations.idiomatic: Shaoxing 31, fifth month, xinmao: word of the emperor’s death reached the court.

sentences.zh: 七月己丑，上尊諡曰恭文順德仁孝皇帝，廟號欽宗。

translations.literal: Seventh month, day jichou: the posthumous title Respectful, Cultured, Shun, Virtuous, Benevolent, and Filial Emperor was granted, with temple name Qinzong.
translations.idiomatic: Seventh month, jichou: he received the posthumous title Respectful, Cultured, Shun, Virtuous, Benevolent, and Filial Emperor and temple name Qinzong.

sentences.zh: 三十二年閏二月戊寅，祔於太廟。

translations.literal: Year 32, intercalary second month, day wuyin: he was enshrined in the Imperial Ancestral Temple.
translations.idiomatic: Year 32, intercalary second month, wuyin: he was enshrined in the Imperial Ancestral Temple.

sentences.zh: 贊曰：帝在東宮，不見失德。

translations.literal: Appraisal: When the emperor was crown prince, no moral failing was seen.
translations.idiomatic: Appraisal: As crown prince he showed no moral failing.

sentences.zh: 及其踐阼，聲技音樂一無所好。

translations.literal: When he took the throne, he had no fondness for sound, skill, or music.
translations.idiomatic: On the throne he cared nothing for sound, skill, or music.

sentences.zh: 靖康初政，能正王黼、朱勔等罪而竄殛之，故金人聞帝內禪，將有卷甲北旆之意矣。

translations.literal: In Jingkang’s early government he could rectify the crimes of Wang Pu and Zhu Mian and exile and execute them, so when the Jin heard of the inner abdication they meant to roll up armor and turn their banners north.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Jingkang he punished Wang Pu and Zhu Mian and drove them into exile or death, so Jin, hearing of the abdication, meant to pack up and march north.

sentences.zh: 惜其亂勢已成，不可救藥，君臣相視，又不能同力協謀，以濟斯難，惴惴然講和之不暇。

translations.literal: Alas, disorder was already formed and beyond saving by medicine; ruler and ministers looked at one another yet could not together plan to rescue this disaster, anxiously having no leisure but to negotiate peace.
translations.idiomatic: Yet chaos was already beyond remedy; ruler and ministers could only stare at one another, unable to join in one plan, and in dread had time for nothing but peace talks.

sentences.zh: 卒致父子淪胥，社稷蕪茀。

translations.literal: In the end father and son were both lost and the state altars lay overgrown.
translations.idiomatic: At last father and son were both lost and the altars lay in weeds.

sentences.zh: 帝至於是，蓋亦巽懦而不知義者歟！

translations.literal: The emperor at this point—was he perhaps timid and submissive, not knowing righteousness?
translations.idiomatic: Was the emperor by then simply timid and unrighteous?

sentences.zh: 享國日淺，而受禍至深，考其所自，真可悼也夫！

translations.literal: His days on the throne were short yet the calamity he suffered was deep; examine where it came from—truly lamentable!
translations.idiomatic: He reigned briefly yet suffered deeply; trace the cause and it is truly lamentable!

sentences.zh: 真可悼也夫！

translations.literal: Truly lamentable!
translations.idiomatic: Truly lamentable!
